reason: E2 states laser cladding produces coatings with low porosity, no cracks, and good metallurgical bonding, supporting the first premise. E1 shows RHEA coatings on TC4 can have fine dendritic microstructures, supporting the second premise. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides direct evidence of significantly increased hardness or wear resistance for RHEA coatings on TC4, nor do they mention controlled Ti addition for compatibility, leaving the third and fourth premises unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Laser cladding can produce dense, metallurgically bonded RHEA coatings on TC4 with low porosity and no cracks
RHEA coatings on TC4 can achieve fine, coherent microstructures with well-distributed phases
RHEA coatings on TC4 significantly increase surface hardness and wear resistance compared to untreated TC4
Controlled Ti addition in the RHEA coating promotes metallurgical bonding and microstructural compatibility with the TC4 substrate
